ask.description: the model was asked here, from the prefix ending at `through`; what the provider keeps about it is stored in that provider's own component beside this one

through.description: the last entry of the prefix it was asked with

attempt.description: Provider request lifecycle. Unfinished dispatched attempts are ambiguous on restart, never automatically replayed.

attention.description: an entry to be read before the next ask

brief.description: the session’s own account of itself, written at the end and quoted in the next one

cancel.description: an entry that withdraws an earlier one

checkpoint.description: everything through this entry is settled: a compaction boundary

claim.description: a session’s lock on the entity it is stored on

session.description: the session holding it — when that session’s entity dies the lock goes and the entity lives

at.description: when it was taken — stamped when the lock is new

conflict.description: two sessions wanted one thing: written after the refusal, never by a client

loser.description: the session whose write was refused

holder.description: the session that already held the lock

dispatch.description: a child's place under the bound on children: queued, active, waiting on its own, or settled; it survives a restart

entry.description: one entry of a transcript; the component stored beside it is its kind

seq.description: Positive integer position; omit on append to allocate atomically. Explicit fractional or occupied positions are refused.

fork.description: this session continues another transcript from one of its entries

from.description: the entry this fork continues from: the parent's entries up to it are this transcript's prefix

imported.description: an entry imported from somewhere else — which source, and which line of it

notice.description: passive transcript context, included in the next ask without requesting one

task.description: the task that prompted this notice

reasoning.description: an entry the model reasoned with rather than returned

resume.description: set aside by an actor to come back to, with its place in the stack

session.description: a transcript something reacts to. Identity only: what it is doing is read off its entries (`status`), where it runs is @yaks/process `process`, and what it was asked for is the `using` on its first entry

id.description: the runner’s own id for it

actor.description: who it speaks as — the identity that survives a /clear, where `created.via` is the run

operator.description: true when a person is driving this transcript rather than an agent

standing.description: a long-running session: recorded here rather than ended when its work is done

status.description: what the newest entry implies: pending is waiting on the model, running is waiting on an answer, settled has nothing to do

spawned.description: a child session delegated by a parent; fork independently selects an inherited prefix

stop.description: a marker in the transcript: the runner does nothing after it

using.description: provider, model and effort: on an input it sets or switches them, on an ask it records what was served

provider.description: the provider asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still records what answered it

model.description: the model asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still records what answered it

instructions.description: system instructions in force for this transcript

claim_take.title: Claim an entity
claim_take.description: Reserve a stored record (entity) for an agent work session so another session cannot claim it. This reservation is a claim or lease: writing one over another session’s claim fails the whole batch, so release first. The same session claiming again is a no-op refresh. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

target.description: the entity to claim; any entity at all; pass its id or registered name

session.description: the session that holds the claim (default: the caller’s session); pass its id or registered name

claim_release.title: Release a claim
claim_release.description: Remove the reservation (claim) held by an agent work session on a stored record (entity). Deliberately unguarded: releasing is how a claim is handed over, and a dead session’s claims are released by whichever process notices first. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

target.description: the entity whose claim to release; pass its id or registered name

session_context.title: Read a session’s context
session_context.description: At the start of an agent work session, find or create its stored session record. Pass the id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or a hook containing session_id. Returns the session record changes and text in content.body naming the session and records it holds claims (work reservations) on, for the harness to inject. An explicit session argument takes precedence over the hook. With no session id, including a malformed hook without an explicit id, returns nothing and makes no changes.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing session_id; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

actor.description: id or name of the persistent identity this session acts as, retained when the agent clears its conversation

session_wrap.title: Wrap up a session
session_wrap.description: At the end of an agent work session, save the optional brief (its own account of what it did) and release every claim, or work reservation, it still holds. Pass a session id or a hook containing session_id. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and field groups) for the brief and claim removals. If the session does not exist or no id is supplied, returns nothing and makes no changes.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing session_id; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

brief.description: what this session did, in its own words

session_listen.title: Listen for a session’s work
session_listen.description: Print one line for each thing addressed to an agent work session as it arrives: a comment on a stored record (entity) the session has claimed, a knock at the session or at that record, a letter delivered to it. Each item is marked notified once printed, so it is printed once, including anything that arrived while nothing was listening; the session’s own writes are never printed. Meant for a command line under a monitor that reads each printed line as an event, such as Claude Code’s Monitor tool: `yak session listen --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`. Does not return while the process is up.

session.description: the session to listen for (default: the caller’s session); pass its id or registered name

session_brief.title: Record a session’s brief
session_brief.description: Save an agent work session’s brief: its own account of what it did. Replaces any previous brief; creates a session record if needed. Pass text and either session or a hook containing session_id. Returns the session id and written fields as a JSON bundle. This stores the brief but does not itself inject it into another session.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing session_id; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

hooks_install.title: Install the lifecycle hooks
hooks_install.description: Write SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks (commands run when an agent session starts or ends) into a Claude-compatible harness settings file, so every session starts by reading its context back (session_context) and ends by wrapping up (session_wrap). The turns in between are read from the harness's own transcript file by the package's duty. Replaces an earlier install, including the turn hooks an older one wrote, and leaves every other entry in the file alone. Writes to the machine the tool runs on. Returns a text confirmation naming the settings path. Pass remove: true to uninstall just these hooks.

yak.description: the path to the yak command on this machine

remove.description: remove the entries instead of writing them

claim_check.title: Check for stale claims
claim_check.description: Check for work reservations (claims) on records (entities) whose agent session is over: a holder this graph has no session entity for, or one whose session stopped or failed. Otherwise the board reports somebody working on what nobody is working on. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

session_check.title: Check for stalled sessions
session_check.description: Check that no session has stalled: waiting on a turn or a tool answer for hours with nothing appended. Uses the server’s stall threshold (two hours by default) for pending or running sessions. A stopped background process can leave such a session without an answer. Reports when timestamps are unavailable to make that judgment. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

session_run.description: run a transcript until it has nothing more to do: a `using` on an entry asks for a turn, a stop ends it (and gives up a child's place), a child is admitted, or a task a transcript holds completes, is cancelled or loses a dependency
